definition: Apocryphal means of doubtful authenticity, widely circulated but almost certainly untrue, though often retold as if true.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word apocryphal. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know apocryphal should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The tale that the young general wept because there were no more worlds to conquer is probably apocryphal, but writers have retold it for centuries.
An embellished account stretches real events with extra flourishes, while an apocryphal one is almost certainly not true at all, no matter how often it is retold.
An apocryphal legend grows up innocently around something people want to believe, but a fabricated story is invented outright, usually with the intent to deceive.

Dubious means of doubtful truth or reliability - a dubious claim invites suspicion but the verdict is still open. Apocryphal is more specific and more settled: it describes a story that is almost certainly untrue yet keeps circulating because people enjoy retelling it. A dubious rumor awaits judgment; an apocryphal legend has survived it.

Unverified means no one has confirmed the claim yet - the checking simply has not been done, so the truth is still open. Apocryphal goes further: the story has been examined, is almost certainly untrue, and circulates anyway. An unverified report awaits evidence; an apocryphal tale has outlived the evidence against it.

Apocryphal means of doubtful authenticity, widely circulated but almost certainly untrue, though often retold as if true.
Every summer, tour guides in the harbor town repeat the story that a celebrated novelist wrote her most famous chapter in a single afternoon at the corner cafe.
A local historian finally checked ship manifests, hotel registers, and the novelist's own letters, and found she had never visited the town at all.
The cafe keeps its brass plaque anyway.
The story is apocryphal: widely retold, fondly believed, and almost certainly untrue.
The cafe story is a charming tale that people keep retelling in good faith even though the evidence shows it almost certainly never happened, which is exactly what apocryphal means.
literary, journalistic register
Apocryphal attaches to stories, quotations, and origin tales (an apocryphal anecdote, an apocryphal deathbed quip).
It implies a legend retold in good faith because people enjoy believing it, which sets it apart from a plain lie told to deceive.

Ask a struggling algebra student for comfort and you may hear that Einstein failed math as a boy.
The story is apocryphal: biographers have checked the school records, and he was in fact at the top of his class.
Einstein himself denied it when a newspaper printed the claim in 1935.
Yet the tale refuses to die, because it is more useful than the truth -- everyone wants genius to have started from failure.
The records survive; the legend simply outruns them.
